newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland government mourns Belfast-born Herzog.
newsitem.headline: Ireland government mourns Belfast-born Herzog.

text.p: The chairman of Ireland's joint foreign affairs committee said on Thursday that former Israeli president Chaim Herzog, who was born in Northern Ireland, was "a distinguished Irishman".
Alan Shatter said in a statement that Herzog, who died aged 78, was a "man of great intellect and dynamism".
Herzog was born in 1918 in Belfast where his father was rabbi of a small Jewish community. He went to British-mandated Palestine in 1935 to study at a Jewish theological school.

"He was sincerely committed to peace and reconciliation between Israel, neighbouring Arab states and Palestinians. His passing will be deeply mourned by all of those who had the privilege of knowing him," Shatter said.
Herzog, a historian and former diplomat, died on Thursday after a long illness at 78. Israeli officials were preparing for a state funeral but a date was not immediately set.
Herzog, a former United Nations ambassador, was the country's president for a decade until 1993 when he was succeeded by President Ezer Weizman.
